kameo-nx: notes for this package
=================================

Ryujinx and the PC are proxies: every timing they give is theirs, not the A57's. Your two console runs are the only real measurements.

New in this package: Kameo: RePowered's four cheat codes. Nothing else changed since rc8.

NOT TESTED. No run has reached them: the emulator test was stopped before its first press, because you are testing them on the console.
The code compiles and the hooks are in the binary. That is all that is known. A wrong address would show up here first.

Enter these on any pause or options page, eight presses. A sound plays when it works.
  Level Select             LB RB LB RB X Y X Y
  Unlock All Extras        X X Y Y LB LB RB RB
  All Warriors & Upgrades  Y X Y X RB LB RB LB
  Collectibles (tracker)   X Y LB RB X Y LB RB

BACK UP YOUR SAVE before you try Level Select. Starting from a task sets the story to that point and saves the game. Collectibles are kept, the story position is not.

What to try, in this order, in gameplay:
1. Pause and enter a code. You should hear the sound.
2. Go into Game Options. There should be an Extras line at the end. With no code entered it must not be there, and that page should look as it always has.
3. Open Extras. Turn Unlock All Extras and All Warriors & Upgrades on and off, and check that the value changes and the cursor stays put.
4. Open Collectibles and check the counts look sensible. B goes back.
5. Open Level Select, pick a chapter, pick a task. The confirmation opens on Cancel. Try Cancel, then Start. The pause should close and the task should load.
6. With All Warriors on, start a level and check the warriors are in the sack. With Unlock All Extras on, look at the extras menu.
7. Turn the console off and on: what you unlocked and turned on should still be there.

What to send me if something goes wrong: which step, what you saw, and renut_001.log. Its lines start "[kameo] cheat code entered" and "[kameo] level select".

Good to know:
- The two cheats only work with banjo_cpu_native_bulk on, which is the default.
- kameo_codes.txt next to the NRO holds what you unlocked. Delete it to start over. kameo_cheat_codes = false in kameo.toml removes the feature.
- Labels are in English only. RePowered's Options pages, its tribe shop sales and its cheat guard (a leaderboard mark and a save backup) are not ported.
- If a code seems to do nothing, it may already be unlocked: a code only plays its sound the first time.

From the last package (rc8), still worth your console's time: your third console run (docs/console-run-3-2026-11-03.md, docs/kameo-notes.md in the source):
- Ten GPU changes, none meant to change a pixel: colour resolves left in the target's image (banjo_deko3d_color_handover), the frame's last
  resolve scanned out with no copy (banjo_deko3d_scanout_handover), depth sampled while a draw only tests it (banjo_deko3d_depth_handover_sampled,
  banjo_deko3d_depth_read_layout), the gamma ramp copied only when it changes (banjo_renut_gamma_upload_once) and in a smaller format, a cheaper scan-out
  (banjo_renut_present_no_pow, banjo_renut_present_texel_load), a register cap on four shaders (banjo_deko3d_gpr32), and fewer target binds
  (banjo_deko3d_resolve_keeps_target). Each is one key in kameo.toml, false to turn it off.
- My estimate: about 1.5 ms of the GPU's 22 ms, not measured. The frame rate in handheld should not change: the drawing thread is the limit.
- Also in here, from the last package: the fourth core and the hand work on the drawing thread. The hand work has now had its first real run
  under the guard: 0 differences in 3.8 million compared calls. Three of those edits cannot be compared: sub_82524E98, sub_820E7F10, sub_820E5100.

Watch for: flickering or wrong shading on soft particles and fog, near where they meet geometry. That is depth being sampled while bound
(banjo_deko3d_depth_handover_sampled = false turns it off), the change the emulator can check least, since it models neither depth compression
nor Zcull. Tell me where it shows. A hitch or missing surface in a menu or a cutscene is the colour hand-over: banjo_deko3d_color_handover = false.

The picture in the emulator: the same set of output levels as the old build in every channel, and wall and lilac within what runs of
the old build vary by. That is not a proof of identical pixels: the scene differs from run to run. An in-run on/off test is the next check.

Cores
-----
In Sphaira, press X on kameo-nx.nro, Install Forwarder, Address Space 39-bit, Create Forwarder. Start that forwarder twice: the first start
writes its four-core NPDM to sdmc:/atmosphere/contents/05E750DF55751000/exefs/main.npdm, and the second has all four. The id is what Sphaira
gives this exact path, sdmc:/switch/kameo-nx/kameo-nx.nro. The log's "[banjo] system core:" line says whether it was granted, and
rex_profile.log's "system core 3: idle N%" what is left of it. Delete that main.npdm to go back to three.
This needs the kameo.toml in this package: an older one on your card has an empty banjo_forwarder_program_id, which overrides the built-in
one. banjo-nx measured stutter when the system had 41-55 % of core 3; here the Audio Worker and compiler should take about 29 %. If sound
stutters with four cores, set banjo_system_core = 0 in kameo.toml and tell me.

Known differences from the reference (docs/kameo-notes.md has the captures): none open in the idle view of Thorn's Castle. The rings
above the player are denser than in the reference: the game places them by frame rate, so your console's spacing will follow its own.

Ryujinx had a bug that made metal in the hole in the wall look mottled lilac. It was in Ryujinx's shader translator, not this build, and
is fixed in the Ryujinx on this PC. A console should not show it: if that metal looks mottled on your console, tell me, because then
this reading is wrong (banjo_gpu_output_trim = false in kameo.toml would be the first test).

No model or level in the game or its DLC uses the tessellated draw command, so banjo-nx's tessellation work is not in this port. If a
later level is missing geometry, tell me where: that scan does not cover draws built directly in code.

Setting up
----------
A package made with -Ready has a switch folder holding everything: copy it to the root of the SD card, merging with the card's
switch folder, and start kameo-nx from the homebrew menu. About 5.7 GB, and about 90 MB more when the DLC installs at the first
start. A card that already has an earlier package needs only two files from switch/kameo-nx: kameo-nx.nro and kameo.toml (keep your
own kameo.toml's changes if you made any). Otherwise:
1. Copy COPY_TO_SD_switch_kameo-nx to sdmc:/switch/kameo-nx/ .
2. game_root/: your extracted disc, with title update 2's default.xexp next to default.xex.
3. update/: title update 2's language folders (English, French ...).
4. dlc/ (optional): the four DLC packages as they came, one copy of the Add-On Pack. Installed at the first start.
5. Start the NRO.

deko3d_shaders.bin holds compiled shaders, built on the PC and merged with what your console compiled; deko3d_shaders.idx is its
index, which only saves time at each start; pipeline_list.bin, from your console run, says which pipelines to build ahead. Delete
any of them to start it over; shaders it lacks are compiled as they come.

Which toml
----------
The NRO reads only kameo.toml, over its built-in settings. (These notes used to say renut.toml: that file does nothing.) The
one here is configs/renut.toml. To use another, copy it from configs/ over kameo.toml.
renut.toml        shipped settings, logs and diagnostics on: use this first. It is what the emulator tests ran, plus their test keys.
renut_play.toml   the same with the render-thread diagnostics off, for playing.
renut_ab.toml     the in-run A/B list, 30 s halves, target 1 as a do-nothing control. A round is 9 minutes and the list starts
                  at boot, so the first round lands partly on menus and loading: get into gameplay, stand still in one place
                  for 25 minutes or more, and send logs/renut_001.log. The "[renut A/B]" lines give each target; read them
                  against target 1's spread. In the emulator that spread was 3 ms, and no target could be judged.
The others        renut_verify.toml (slow; every verify key), renut_profile.toml (sampling profile), renut_pgo.toml, and the
                  options that change the picture, each one key away from renut.toml, for you to decide on.
No kameo.toml     delete it and the NRO writes a short one with the player's options (language, buttons, frame cap) and runs on the
                  built-in settings: the same picture settings as renut.toml, with no log. Not run in the emulator with this NRO.

What to test, in order
----------------------
1. Boot to the title, menus and a new game. Does the Rare logo, the opening movie and Thorn's Castle appear?
2. New Quest's keyboard is the Switch's own (not exercised in the emulator: the tests answer it with its default).
3. Sound in the movie and in gameplay.
4. Frame rate in Thorn's Castle, handheld (720 lines) and docked (1080 lines). Docked at 1080 has not been run at all.
5. A DLC outfit, if the DLC is installed. Never selected in a test so far; Expert no longer refuses for the Power Pack.
6. A 25-minute stay in one place with configs/renut_ab.toml copied over kameo.toml. Target 71 is the question for you: Begin*Vertices draws in the delta chain,
   on here and off in banjo-nx. It removes about 12 MB/s of memcpy from the drawing thread on the PC, and could not be measured
   in the emulator. Target 72 is new: its off half loses the glow on the clouds and should cost almost nothing to keep on.
7. The sky through the window in Thorn's Castle, the first thing to compare against a real 360 or the reference: orange bands on the
   clouds near the sun, cream where the sun itself shows. The colour moves as the clouds do, so look for a few seconds.

Things most likely to go wrong
------------------------------
- banjo_renut_deferred_chain is ON here, against banjo-nx's default, because Kameo has one device. It hung banjo-nx's emulator
  when there were two. If the game freezes after some minutes, set it to false in kameo.toml and tell me whether that cured it.
- GPU memory: the region peaked at 963 MB in the emulator at 720 lines. 1080 docked will use more; the log's "Memory:" lines
  every 10 s say how much.

Turning on a console profile
----------------------------
Copy configs/renut_profile.toml over kameo.toml, play the slow scene for a few minutes, and send logs/rex/rex_profile.log, the
log, and this package's name. kameo-nx.elf and source_<commit>.tgz here are what maps its samples to source lines: keep them
with the NRO. The kameo.toml here already samples, so one run of the same scene as your last compares the two directly.
